The most common win left on "LOTERIA®" is $3. The second biggest prize left is $10,000, and five of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

If "LOTERIA®" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
959.headline: A close look at the prizes

972.body:
Of the unclaimed prize money on "$8 Million Money Maker", most is in wins under $5,000. The game is a game that pays many small prizes and few large ones. That is neither good nor bad, only how it was designed. Choose the kind of game that fits the win you want.

The most common prize left on "$8 Million Money Maker" right now is $100.

Tomorrow's count on "$8 Million Money Maker" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
972.headline: The prize mix in this game

If you play "$1,000,000 Money Rush" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.

976.body:
"100X The Cash" paid out its last $2 million prize close to two months ago. The ticket still advertises it because printed tickets never change. Prize tables do change, and the biggest prize listed today is $10,000.

Everything here about "100X The Cash" comes from official North Carolina lottery numbers, current through November 19.
976.headline: Far less than $2 million to win

988.body:
"Emerald 10's" has had no $1 million top prize claimed since we started watching it. Everyday prizes keep getting claimed, and fewer tickets are left each day. The number of tickets printed is fixed. Each day without a top prize claim leaves those prizes among fewer tickets.

Everything above about "Emerald 10's" comes from the North Carolina Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.

994.body:
The key fact about "$25,000 Triple Play" is how its twelve prize levels are built. The prize money leans toward the smaller prizes. Games built like this give out wins often, but rarely large ones. Prize counts change daily, but this design does not.

The numbers for "$25,000 Triple Play" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
